topicName: Credential Dumping and Hash Cracking (Mimikatz, Hashcat, John the Ripper)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Credential Dumping and Hash Cracking Technical Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covers the theoretical and practical aspects of credential dumping and offline password auditing using industry-standard tools such as Mimikatz, Hashcat, and John the Ripper. This knowledge is essential for penetration testers and security professionals to identify and remediate weak authentication mechanisms."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 1: Credential Dumping with Mimikatz"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mimikatz is a post-exploitation tool that allows administrators to view authentication credentials, interact with Kerberos tickets, and extract plaintext passwords or password hashes from the Windows LSASS (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service) memory."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensure you have local Administrator or SYSTEM privileges on the target Windows system."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Bypass or account for Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions, as raw memory dumping of LSASS is heavily monitored."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"privilege::debug\nsekurlsa::logonpasswords"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"The 'privilege::debug' command elevates Mimikatz to interact with critical OS processes, and 'sekurlsa::logonpasswords' extracts credentials from memory, including NTLM hashes and plaintext passwords if WDigest is enabled."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 2: Offline Brute-Forcing with Hashcat"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once NTLM or Net-NTLM hashes are successfully dumped, attackers or security auditors test their cryptographic strength using high-performance GPU-accelerated hash crackers like Hashcat."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"hashcat -m 1000 -a 0 ntlm_hashes.txt rockyou.txt -O"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-m 1000 specifies the NTLM hash mode."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-a 0 designates a straight dictionary attack."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-O enables optimized kernels for faster cracking speeds on shorter passwords."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Phase 3: Hash Cracking and Rule-Based Attacks with John the Ripper"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"John the Ripper (JtR) is another versatile password security auditing tool. It excels at rule-based attacks, which mutate standard dictionary words using specific logic (e.g., appending numbers, swapping capitalization) to guess user passwords effectively."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"john --format=NT --wordlist=rockyou.txt ntlm_hashes.txt"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"To apply advanced rule-based mutations, you can utilize built-in rules like --rules=Jumbo or custom rule profiles configured in the john.conf file."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Remediation and Defense Strategies"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enable Credential Guard in Windows 10/11 and Windows Server to isolate the LSASS process and prevent memory scraping."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Disable WDigest authentication to stop plaintext password caching in memory."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enforce strong, complex, and long password policies to drastically increase the mathematical difficulty of offline hash cracking."}]
